It is not a desk but a stand that sits atop a desk. It will provide the benefits of a standing desk without the expense and commitment.

The directions are pictorial, something I do not like. They lead to some confusion but then again I am a person who prefers words to illustrations. That being said the installation was not as frustrating as I anticipated.It seems sturdy. Adjusting the stand itself is simple and smooth. Ho weer adjusting the monitors requires fussing with bolts and tools. The work surface is adequate though not especially generous. there is a little wobble when typing in both the raised and lowered position but not enough to be a deal breaker. It doesn't seem completely level though I haven't determined whether it is the desk or the stand. I have chronic back problems and try to get up at least every hour when I am office bound. This desk does help increase standing time. It is easy to work in the standing position, which is somewhat of a surprise . I am still undecided about upgrading to a complete standing desk but am enjoying the benefits by using this stand.

text_fidelity_a:
CHUWI Hi8 8 inch Windows 10/Android 4.4 Dual Boot Tablet PC, with Features of Intel Quad Core, Full HD 19201200 IPS Screen, 2G RAM/32G ROM and Winkey I have only had this tablet for a day, so this is more of a first impression. If my opinion changes, I will update this review.

I was in the market for an inexpensive dual-boot Win10/Android tablet. I researched for about a week, and I am really happy with the choice I made.

What I wanted: A 8 or 10-inch tablet that I could use for web browsing and video streaming. I game and have a nice gaming laptop that I didn't want to lug around for these purposes. I wanted a decent screen that didn't look cheap. Also the ability to play Android games.

This tablet meets all my expectations. Build is solid and feels high quality. Screen is very bright and text is clear. I had no issues getting accounts set up in Android or Win 10. Android is bare bones and has just about nothing pre-installed, which I love. I would absolutely recommend this tablet, especially at this price point.

What you don't get: No video out port. There is a pro version of this tablet if you need that option. You are not doing any major Windows gaming on this. You are not going to run any extremely resource-intensive Windows apps on this. It has a mono speaker so you aren't getting a high-end audio experience with music. If these are things you need, you will have to spend at least six times as much.
text_fidelity_b: CHUWI Hi8 8 inch Windows 10/Android 4.4 Dual Boot Tablet PC, with Features of Intel Quad Core, Full HD 19201200 IPS Screen, 2G RAM/32G ROM and Winkey

GreatShield (3 Pack) Ultra Anti-Glare (Matte) Clear Screen Protector Film for Amazon Kindle Fire (Does Not Fit Kindle Fire HD) I keep being offered this product to review through the "Your Review Helped" emails I get, even though I've already reviewed it through Vine, so I'll take this opportunity to offer an update. The screen smudges easily with the Great Shield protector applied, and it's hard to clean it. I've subsequently had an opportunity to review the Moshi product, and it is hands-down the best of the two. The clarity of the Moshi screen is better than the Great Shield, and it's easier to apply. I've accordingly bumped the Great Shield down to three stars now that I have something better for comparison.

Original review through Amazon Vine:

Okay, like some other reviewers, I had a frustrating experience getting this anti-glare screen protector installed properly on my Kindle Fire. When you buy this three-pack, figure they are giving you two hands-on lessons in how to install it! (Considering I paid over twice as much for just one Zagg screen protector for my Kindle 2, the price for this Fosmon product is still very reasonable.) I had read all the reviews and warnings before I began, and I still ruined my first two.

First, who lives in a "dust-free environment"? You have to be very careful. You should first shake any dust off the protector itself; after I'd failed to install the first two, I used one of the wipes that came with them to wipe down both sides of my last protector to clear it of all packing dust that it arrived with. Then clean your Fire screen, including the cracks around the sides of the screen. Clean it again. And again.

My first effort went very well until I went to remove the #2 (face) plastic. I didn't realize I had to very slowly pull up on the tab to get the top piece started coming away from the actual shield protector before pulling—so I pulled the whole thing off! One down, two to go. On my second effort, I didn't quite get the protector perfectly positioned so I had a very slight overlap on the right-hand side, resulting in a large unattached area. Unusable. The third time, I folded the #1 plastic down halfway, just so I could hold the protector flat above my Fire and not touch the actual protector (to avoid fingerprints), edged the upper right corner in perfectly straight, anchored it across the top, and then let the protector kind of glide itself onto the screen as I pulled off the remaining #1 plastic. I had some larger bubbled areas, but I did not try to use the little cardboard piece to squeegee them out; I used my thumbs to press outward toward the nearest edge. This gave me a near-perfect installation. I carefully removed the #2 plastic, slipped my Fire back into its [[ASIN:B005QBK5V2 rooCASE Dual-View Multi Angle (Black) 100% Genuine Leather Leather Folio Case Cover for Amazon Kindle Fire 7-Inch Android Tablet]], tucked one of the little squares of screen-cleaning cloth behind the Fire for later cleaning use if needed, and it was all good to go.

After regularly fighting the glare from my Kindle Fire, it took me a little while for my eyes to adjust to the difference with the anti-glare shield protector in place, but I LIKE it! Reading is now easier on my eyes, and my [[ASIN:B005EM6IAA GreatShield 2-in-1 Ballpoint Pen and Capacitive Touchscreen Stylus for Amazon Kindle Fire Tablet]] seems to be working with more precision than it was before. Despite the hassles, I do recommend this product and I'm glad I've got it.
text_fidelity_b: GreatShield (3 Pack) Ultra Anti-Glare (Matte) Clear Screen Protector Film for Amazon Kindle Fire (Does Not Fit Kindle Fire HD)

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier I've had problems with Pixmas in the past, mostly having to do with wireless networks and having to reinstall the software over and over to try to get them to hang on to network settings. I can't guarantee that this printer is going to be any better in the long run, but the set-up actually works pretty well if you use the standard version, not the WPS... and I'm getting way ahead of myself on this one.

To begin with, the printer requires a lot of time for set-up. You're not going to be doing this on the fly, so set aside an hour or so to: 1) remove all the tape of which there is much, 2) read over the instructions 3) install the ink, 4) run a print alignment 5) set up your wireless connection (about which more in a moment) 6) install the software (which takes a good 15 minutes or more), and 7) put the machine (and yourself) through its paces. Yeah, it's going to take a while.

Now I know you can read about the features on your own, so I'm here to tell you about the things that work for me and those that don't. First off, the wireless set-up is confusing. Choose Standard instead of WPS and save yourself some headaches unless you're a computer whiz kid. After the third error message in the WPS set-up I went to standard, entered my pass code and had the connection up and running in about a minute.

Once that was done and the software was installed I fired up the Canon Image Garden. First I scanned an image and attempted to rotate, crop and fix any deficiencies I found. The scan was over sharp and looked a bit jagged, but a little fiddling with the Canon software fixed that. Canon software also rotated and cropped perfectly. One really nice feature is that they remind you to put the printing side of the paper down in the paper cassette. How many pieces of paper will that save?

The biggest complaint I had was that it didn't give me a choice of which paper cassette to use for printing, so I got a ridiculously truncated image on the first try. I believe it chooses the paper based on the size of the image, which I get, but at the same time that limits flexibility in printing. I opened another photo processing program and it allowed me to print from whatever cassette I liked. Coupled with a better suite of applications for correction and enhancement, I think it's safe to say that I'll be using the Canon software almost never.

Printing on plain paper is clearly not going to be as satisfactory as it is on glossy, but in some cases I found it surprisingly good, good enough to give you an idea of what sort of image you're going to end up with when you switch to photo paper. It's also more than good enough for printing out emails and web pages.

Scanning and printing are both pretty fast, another plus. And the copy function works pretty seamlessly without any sort of computer interface. Just punch a couple of buttons and Bob's your uncle! It does take a bit of time to warm up and is a little noisy but no more so than any Canon printer I've ever used. It's not bothersome, in my opinion. You might feel otherwise.

Inks are easy to install, but you'll find refills pricey, no question. I suspect off-brand ones are available or will be soon enough.

In short, it's a good, inexpensive printer for a home or home office. Use photo paper and settings and get the full quality the MG5420 is capable of producing; I think it's pretty remarkable. The photos I printed out are as good as or in one case, better than the original. That's a powerful recommendation in my book.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier

text_fidelity_a:
Stanley 33959 ShopMax Power Hub 20-Feet 4-Outlet Cord Reel , Yellow Why is the cable size and breaker on this thing so undersized when it is presumably (due to the fact that it is Stanley Max) for running power tools? 16AWG and 13A is actually a bottleneck compared to a standard 15A 14AWG household circuit. Worse is that it is a huge bottleneck compared to the 12AWG 20A circuits I put in work and kitchen areas to accommodate the many tools (e.g., miter saws, medium sized air compressors, etc.) and appliances (e.g., microwaves) that push the envelope on the 15A circuits.

Point is, right off the bat, I can't run large tools on this thing (and that includes some plug-in-lawn equipment), and I can't run most medium sized tools two at a time on this thing (good drills, planers, grinders, etc. often draw around 9A), so what's the point of the multiple outlets except, granted, that you don't have to unplug one to plug the other in over and over again if working with two tools alternately.

On the flip side, this lighter gauge cable does allow this power hub to be lighter and easier to deal with. It does roll up nicely and I like that the cord can be attached on the side so it doesn't unravel itself.

But I think the outlets should be spaced a little further a part, given that the size could accommodate that. That would allow larger plugs, and maybe even some AC adapters to fit. I also think 20 ft. is way too short, especially for the reel setup (it's not that hard to untangle 20ft.) and the fact that this thing is probably large enough to hold more.

You could use it for Christmas lights or something like that - except it is not a true weatherproof cord - or some low power hobby in the house. This has no quality issues, and there are plenty of uses for it, but the name has me thinking it is trying to be in the tool market. To be really effective in that market, it should be 12AWG, accept 20A plugs, be minimum 50' long, and have the outlets spaced slightly further apart.
text_fidelity_b: Stanley 33959 ShopMax Power Hub 20-Feet 4-Outlet Cord Reel , Yellow

Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th] My title pretty much sums it up - I love the Kindle Paperwhite! I am a big reader, but I resisted the e-reader obsession until December 2010 when I gave into a Nook. Back then I decided on a Nook because the Kindle did not allow you to borrow books from the library, which was a deal breaker for me.

Fast-forward two and a half years... My Nook was getting older and the discrepancy between prices and availability of e-books between Amazon and Barnes & Noble was becoming increasingly clearer. Also, I love Amazon as a general rule, and order from them pretty heavily for a variety of items, so it made sense to switch over. After brief research, I stumbled upon the Kindle Paperwhite. It met all of my requirements - a dedicated e-reader (no tablet for me, thanks), with a built in light. Yippee! My hubby and puppy (okay, just the hubby) purchased the Kindle Paperwhite for my birthday at the end of August and it was love at first sight. It is unreasonable to compare the Kindle Paperwhite to my old Nook, so I won't. I can freely admit that most of my love comes from the new technology and association with Amazon. I love the light. It is awesome to not have to use a clip on light at night. They are usually terrible and not evenly spaced. The light makes reading at night a breeze. Plus, it is a perfect light, so it really is like reading a book and not like reading on a backlit screen (a la the iPhone or iPad). I love the ease of purchasing books from Amazon, and I love their prices and special deals. But, most of all, I love checking out library books! The very thing that turned me away from the Kindle initially is now the best. There is no need to connect my Kindle to a laptop to download a book. Yay! I can just wirelessly send a book to my Kindle, the same as purchasing one. You must be a wireless network (not 3G), but that my dear friends is a tiny issue. Overall, I love my Kindle Paperwhite and I cannot think of one single thing to make it better! Love it.

Helpful tips - 3G or not? I love the 3G, but it's not a necessity if you have wide access to wireless. I would definitely say to go for the ads, however. They are entirely inoffensive and unobtrusive. They only come up when your Kindle is asleep. Save the $20 and buy yourself a few books!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th]

text_fidelity_a:

Granted, I'm not an audiophile so I can't judge all the nuances, but regardless if I'm listening to music or watching a movie, the sound quality is absolutely wonderful. Plus, there are lots of ways to customize the sound to your liking.

I debated between the Onkyo and a similarly-spec'd Denon. I opted for the Onkyo since I've had Onkyo receivers in the past that never failed on me. In contrast, I have had to replace 2 Denon's due to failure (one completely died; the other had a very temperamental on/off button and would no longer respond to any remote control commands).

Setup is straightforward. The hardest part is connecting all the speakers. One of these days I'm going to get banana plus for them, but until then it's a pain getting all the wires properly set. The installation program walks you through the audio testing/calibration (using the supplied microphone), getting online, and other setup processes. I didn't encounter any problems. The firmware update process also went smoothly (had the receiver download it online).

I'm very impressed with all the features, the performance and the build quality. Excellent value for the price, and I would highly recommend this model.
text_fidelity_b: Onkyo TX-RZ620 7.2 Channel Network A/V Receiver

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) I use earbuds a lot since I typically prefer the lightness and ease of use compared with traditional headphones. Right out of the box these were a bit puzzling as to how to position them for use. But, after a bit of fiddling with the over-the-ear loop, it becomes clear.

The in-ear comfort is good. It comes with a variety of ear tips including two types I’ve not used before: a double flange silicon tip and a triple flange silicon tip. The flanges allow the ear bud to make a much better seal in your ear canal. That not only helps cut out ambient noise intruding, it also improves the bass response. I found the double flange works best for me, but the variety of tips included appears sufficient to fit pretty much any ear.

It also comes with an excellent case for storage, and adapters for airplane use and for 1/4 inch plugs. I especially like the case since it’s small enough to make it easy to carry along (roughly 3.5 inches by 3 by 1.5 inches thick) and is reinforced to avoid being crushed. It has mesh pockets to keep everything stowed, and looks nice to boot (black with red contrast in the middle). All-in-all, it’s a great kit in terms of useful accessories.

I’m not as pleased with the cord. While I like how sturdy it is, it has a “Y” link that always seems to be in the way when I’m working out. I got used to it eventually, but a more streamlined cord system would have been a better design approach. Another negative is the 3.5mm plug. It needs to be seated just so or you get sound cut-outs or static. I tried it with several devices to be sure the issue is with the plug and not the device. A more robust plug is needed for this – you shouldn’t have to fiddle with it to get it to seat properly.

The over-the-ear loops are also a bit annoying at first. Granted, that’s certainly due to the fact that I usually use standard in-ear buds without the loop, so any type of loop feels weird to me at first. The material is soft and bendy, so you can position it in any variety of ways. It could benefit from some additional padding. On the plus side, they do hold the buds in very well. Quick head movements that would have loosened an in-ear bud didn’t jar these loose at all.

Now for the really important feature: how they sound. In a word, excellent. My benchmark for moderately-priced earbuds has been units made by RHA out of the UK. These sound nearly as good. Very clean sound but still ample bass provided that you select the right tip. For me, the standard tip (the one installed as delivered) gave me very little in terms of bass. Selecting a different tip to provide a better ear fit did wonders for bass response.

They are a bit more airy than the RHA sound. That could be a plus or a minus depending on your preferred type of music. Very heavy bass music is not a good match for these. Pretty much everything else is, and I appreciated the enhanced clarity. It’s the type of sound that, when you hear it, the first word that would come to mind is “clean.”

They look odd, make take you a moment to figure out how to position them, but provide a very open, natural sound. It comes with a well-designed kit of useful extras. However, the plug issues, the cord, and the ear loops collectively knock it down a star. Still well worth considering, however, and I would certainly recommend them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher Price Precious Planet Whale of a Tub We purchased this product before we were expecting, knowing that it was neutral gendered and would be perfect for a boy or a girl. When we had our first child, a 9 lb, 11 oz baby girl, I was SO nervous! I didn't know a thing about babies. My eldest sister helped me give her her first bath and complimented our whale tub. She said it was so nice that the green padding in the base would help prevent baby from slipping. By the third bath, I had it down.

As the weeks have gone on, our little one has really loved her tub. She began holding her head up at 4 days old and was doing so independently within a month of her birth. She loved kicking and splashing in her tub. She has never cried in the bath. We use a turtlemeter thermometer and she thinks of it like a little toy with which to play.

I would recommend this tub with the seat in it for a newborn baby up to about 12 lbs. Once our daughter was 13 lbs, she has trouble staying warm in the tub with the seat attached. It simply wasn't deep enough for her while she was lying down and she only got her bottom half wet unless I poured water over her, and the chilly air would then make her cold.

With the seat out, she needs to be sitting on her own so there was a two month gap where we did not use her tub, and instead bathed her with me in the big tub.

Once she was a successful sitter, we returned her to this tub for warmer nights, so she could sit and play in the water. She loves it!

After a bath, I would recommend not only using the drain in the tub, but turning this whale tub upside-down and and then turning it from side-to-side to drain it, as the water tends to get trapped beneath the green padded area. You can also remove the seat to clean under it. Using dish soap and a scrub daddy sponge, I am able to quickly clean the tub in-between uses.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher Price Precious Planet Whale of a Tub

text_fidelity_a:
Sony A90J 65 Inch TV: BRAVIA XR OLED 4K Ultra HD Smart Google TV with Dolby Vision HDR and Alexa Compatibility XR65A90J- 2021 Model The box took a big gouge in shipping (in just the original TV box), but the TV was fine, so packaging is probably adequate. Unboxing was easy and there was just a bit of styrofoam and minimal cardboard. Be careful with removing the television from the box, because these things are getting thin enough to be bent under their own weight.

It mounted fine on my old wall mount, but required a different screw size. The screws from my previous setup were the wrong size, so you might want to check what you've got and order some so you don't have to wait around.

There isn't much thought put into cable management, so you'll have to come up with your own solution if you don't want cords visible. Power cord is in the lower right quadrant. Most of the other cords are in the lower left, as is a well hidden power button on the back left. The instructions are minimal. I tried hooking my receiver in as instructed to use the television speaker in place of my old center speaker, but it wouldn't work. It may have just been a clash of brands and standards, because every time I tried to switch to using the TV speakers in the options, it would shut off my Pioneer receiver instead. I ended up using the other speaker input, which did work. I can't believe we're in the 2020's and still cramming bare wires in as audio input. I've got a drawer full of various audio cables here.

Turning it on, I was greeted with setup options. The remote seems high quality, but I wish it had some air-remote functionality. Navigating menus with buttons can get a bit confusing. After getting it hooked up to wifi, I was off to YouTube to find something to make sure it was working right before I hooked everything else up. One of those HD coral reef relaxation videos was just the thing. The picture is vibrant! Bright and colorful. The bezels aren't small enough to tile these together, but are very small. My kids wouldn't let me change the video for hours. They just sat and watched the fish. I'm susceptible to the whine some televisions put out, and I've heard none of that. Worked great for video games, though I didn't try anything especially high end. Worked well for computer output. With the exception of that one audio jack compatibility issue, and the different sized screws, everything has worked as expected.

The screen is a speaker, like a modern smartphone. Sound is good, especially at frequencies you would hear from a center speaker. I definitely still wanted my subwoofer and side speakers to round things out, but it's really nice to have the voices from the television coming from where the faces are, not from some speaker below the television.

I don't have a different brand of 2021 television to compare it to, but my impression is that there is a bit of a premium for the brand name, but it's a very nice product. This was certainly an upgrade for me. A lot of progress has been made in the 8 years since I last upgraded.
text_fidelity_b: Sony A90J 65 Inch TV: BRAVIA XR OLED 4K Ultra HD Smart Google TV with Dolby Vision HDR and Alexa Compatibility XR65A90J- 2021 Model

text_fidelity_a:
Sony BDP-S350 1080p Blu-Ray Disc Player I've had my Sony S350 Blu-Ray player for over a year now and here are my thoughts. The picture is completely amazing, even makes regular dvd's look better. I love that there's no more cords for picture and more cords for sound, just one HDMI cable and poof - high quality picture and surround sound.

A couple things to consider before buying your Blu-Ray player and subsequent Blu-Ray discs:
1. Blu-Ray will play your regular dvd's but if you have a regular dvd player (such as in your car) you cannot play Blu-Ray discs in it.

2. Patience is needed with this unit. After putting in a movie, especially if it is somewhat new, it could take 3-5 minutes to load. I am personally never in that much of a hurry to start the movie. While the movie is loading (a progress/status bar is provided on-screen) I can make popcorn, get the dogs situated, etc.

3. In conjunction with #2, the owner of this player must also be diligent about updating the firmware inside the player. I updated my player once last year (in November) and have noticed slower loads with current movies, so I plan to update it again next month (March). My guess is that it's good to update it 1-2 times per year.
What's involved in updating the firmware? I log onto a blu-ray firmware site, choose my model of player, then burn the update to a dvd disc. Place the disc in the player, it will read and update your firmware (took mine about 5-10 minutes as I remember). Afterward, your player will load movies more quickly.
Note: Loading never occurs during the movie, the only load-time that is experienced comes immediately after inserting the disc. Here's an example of the patience it takes to operate this blu-ray player:
Turn the player on - wait about 30 seconds for the unit to be able to receive or eject a disc (if you're trying to quickly eject a disc and run it back to the movie store, this can seem long!)
Insert disc and close - wait 3-5 minutes for movie menu to load

After that, you're set to go. For me, it's worth the wait and the trouble to keep it updated. I am quite sure that future models will require less patience and diligence, but for now this is the way it is. If you want extremely good quality with your movies, it's a wonderful addition to your home theater.
text_fidelity_b: Sony BDP-S350 1080p Blu-Ray Disc Player

Logitech G240 Cloth Gaming Mouse Pad for Low-DPI Gaming I'm not a gamer. I wanted to try this mouse pad out for graphics (photo editing, vector graphics, and so forth). I'm not a big fan of pen-type tablet input devices. I've always preferred working with a mouse. (To me, the only real down side to using a mouse instead of a tablet input is loss of pressure sensitivity, but there are plenty of workarounds.)

This pad works great. An optical/laser mouse reads it very well, with the slightest movements picked up. The bottom of the pad is grippy enough for the pad to stay put, and the surface, while satin-like, still has enough resistance to provide a lot of fine control.

It's also larger than I expected. It's 11 inches by 13.5 inches. And it is quite flexible and rolls up easily for storage or transport.

Here are some tips for getting precise mouse control:

First of all understand that a low-DPI setting means your pointer doesn't move far when you move the mouse. This enables gamers to aim and target precisely in-game. It also enables artists to precisely move the pointers when working on graphics. How far your cursor/pointer moves is entirely up to you and can be adjusted in your control panel for pointer settings (or, depending on the game, possibly can be adjusted in your game settings).

In that control panel, uncheck "enhance pointer precision." This will turn off pointer acceleration, which can adversely affect control. If the software (or game) you're using overrides this (rare in graphics software, but more common in games), you may have to employ a fix. Just do a search for "Windows 7/8 mouse fix" and you'll find plenty of information on how to do this.

Anyway, it's a great pad for precision cursor control with a mouse, whether for gaming or graphics.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G240 Cloth Gaming Mouse Pad for Low-DPI Gaming

text_fidelity_a:
Plantronics 211856-99 Backbeat Fit 3100 True Wireless Earbuds, Sweatproof and Waterproof In Ear Workout Headphones, Grey There are "true wireless" earbuds on Amazon for half of this price, but I have tried several of them and they all suffer from poor-to-mediocre sound quality as well as poor battery life. These Plantronics earbuds cost more, but they have great sound quality as well as great battery life. I hear a good amount of bass as well as good clarity in the higher frequencies. My favorite music sounds muddy on cheaper wireless earbuds, but sounds great on these. 5 hour battery life per charge is almost double what the cheap earbuds give me. The ear hooks look clunky, but they are very comfortable and never fall off when I'm jogging or working out.

As with all "true wireless" earbuds, you have to control them with a series of short and long taps on the sides of the earbuds (to change volume, skip around in your music, answer phone calls, etc). If you have a hard time remembering all those commands (as I do), you can always pull out your phone and do the same thing from there.

If you cannot afford "true wireless" earbuds at this price level, my advice is to forget the "true wireless" design and look at Bluetooth earbuds that have a wire connecting the two sides. That style is slightly uglier than "true wireless" but has much better battery life and sound quality for similar price levels and there are pretty good products for much cheaper prices than the "true wireless" design.

I see some review complaints about connectivity and charging problems. My earbuds have worked perfectly with no dropouts, etc. As with any electronic gadget, there is always the possibility of a manufacturing flaw. I would definitely return a product that did not work flawlessly.

Note that this particular Plantronics model is not noise-cancelling or noise-isolating. You will hear some background noise, which is safer if you use them when walking or working in a busy environment. Plantronics does sell noise cancelling earbuds that you could choose instead if that feature is useful and important to you.
text_fidelity_b: Plantronics 211856-99 Backbeat Fit 3100 True Wireless Earbuds, Sweatproof and Waterproof In Ear Workout Headphones, Grey

Samsung 970 EVO Plus SSD 2TB NVMe M.2 Internal Solid State Hard Drive, V-NAND Technology, Storage and Memory Expansion for Gaming, Graphics w/ Heat Control, Max Speed, MZ-V7S2T0B/AM Modern computers are a lot more reliable than computers from 10 or 20 years ago. Computers are not getting a lot faster every year like they used to. I no longer replace my computer every couple of years. If your computer is getting a little sluggish, instead of replacing the whole thing, you can usually give it a huge performance boost by upgrading just key components. In particular, upgrade your memory and upgrade your hard drive. This SSD does not add a lot of capacity, but it gives you a lot of speed so that programs or databases that you use a lot will load much more quickly.

This drive installed and formatted easily on my Windows 10 desktop computer. It's been running flawlessly since then and the performance has been blazingly fast.

There are a lot of different SSDs on the market these days. Check your computer manufacturer's website to see what is compatible with your motherboard. This SSD costs 2 to 3 times as much as entry-level products with the same capacity. The more advanced design makes it more than twice as fast as more basic SSDs. If you use your computer for computer-aided design, graphics/video editing, or hard-core gaming, then the speed may be worth the price to you. For general purpose office or home computing, the entry-level SSDs are probably fine for you.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 970 EVO Plus SSD 2TB NVMe M.2 Internal Solid State Hard Drive, V-NAND Technology, Storage and Memory Expansion for Gaming, Graphics w/ Heat Control, Max Speed, MZ-V7S2T0B/AM

WAVLINK USB 3.0 Universal Docking Station with DVI/HDMI Dual Monitor Docking Station,2 USB 2.0 Port,2 USB 3.0 Port,Gigabit Ethernet,Quick Charging,Supports for Windows Mac OS The links on their site for the software download were not working, so I ended up having to go directly to DisplayPort to download the update. After that it was pretty smooth sailing.

I have kiddo all hooked up with dual monitors and his laptop docked and stored. So, now he has actual room at his desk to put his notebook or textbook or whatever else he needs for school, without the laptop taking up half his space.

To avoid any latency issues you can sometimes get while gaming and using DisplayPort software, I did hook his main monitor up directly to his laptop and "mirrored" the screen. This is the one he will play his games on. For his second monitor used for videos, research, etc. I used the HDMI port on the Wavlink dock and "extended" the screen. This way he can have dual monitors and bypass any latency issues that sometimes can crop up. If you can, it is also recommend when gaming to plug the mouse directly into the laptop as well, rather than the dock.

Personally, I don't notice any latency issues on either monitor or when the mouse is hooked up through the dock. But it was easy enough to just bypass the issue all together by how I plugged stuff in. The only struggles I had were with setting up his laptop to not go into hibernate instead of sleep after 2 hours, to stop disabling power to USBs while in sleep, and to allow his keyboard to wake the system out of sleep even though it was clearly already set up to do so. But that is nothing to do with the dock, and everything to do with Windows 10 being a pain in the behind sometimes. Finally everything is all set up, behaving as it should and we are ready for school to start next week. Well I'm ready, him... not so much.
text_fidelity_b: WAVLINK USB 3.0 Universal Docking Station with DVI/HDMI Dual Monitor Docking Station,2 USB 2.0 Port,2 USB 3.0 Port,Gigabit Ethernet,Quick Charging,Supports for Windows Mac OS

Match this flash with the D5000, a $75.00 Stroboframe camera flip bracket, a $50.00 Nikon flash cable (don't get the cable with the focus assist)and pick up a $17.00 Sto-Fen Omni Bounce designed for this flash. You'll have a fully capable flash system. You won't regret it.

For moving around very crowed clubs, photojournalism, and the like, I can't think of a more capable, comfortable, and affordable camera outfit.

Don't worry about the lack of controls on the flash itself. The way the D5000 and this flash functions together will please you much. Especially if you are use to constantly adjusting and setting an external shoe mount flash. The flash is fully controllable from the camera.

Also, you don't have to worry for the safety of the flash as much when mounted on a bracket (or the camera) when moving through crowds.

Compared to a $200.00 to $300.00 flash, getting this flash for your Nikon D5000 only makes good sense.

I'm very happy with the M68. Five stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord For the price this is a very nice USB microphone, I would agree with other reviewers that it performs on par with or better than similar competing USB condenser mics in this price range such as Blue Snowball or the Behringer C1.

I do wish it came with more accessories though similar to the non-USB version. The Aokeo AK-60 XLR version comes with a scissor boom arm, shock mount and pop filter for the same price.. so if you do happen to have a compatible audio interface with phantom power then I would recommend the XLR version.

The main annoyance with this mic is that when using it in windows 10 the driver does not have native mic gain control option. In many recording programs you can boost the mic gain via other means but if using this mic for gaming or other purposes through the native drivers then you will have to be very close to the mic to produce adequate volume (ie you pretty much need a boom arm) or otherwise you will need to boost gain via external passthrough program such as APO equalizer. I have also tried this mic in linux and the drivers there do have native gain control.

Overall I do think the sound quality and construction of the mic is good for the price and I would recommend it .. just note that if using windows 10 you will probably either need a boom arm or need to use external software to boost the mic gain. A boom arm is strongly recommended anyways to prevent extraneous noises like keyboard clacking, etc..
text_fidelity_b: Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord

text_fidelity_a:
VIZIO Sound Bar for TV, 28” 2.1 Surround Sound System for TV with Wireless Subwoofer and Bluetooth, Channel Home Theater Sound Bar – Remote SB2821-D6 The first delivery had subwoofer that was dead on arrival. No power.

They sent a replacement. It works great. Music streaming from my phone or computer by bluetooth sounds great. Better than my Bose.

If you want instruction on how to operate this thing properly look at the copied review below. This was helpful.

One other or two were somewhat helpful.

The instructions they put in the package gets the thing on but doesn't tell you how to operate it.

FYI:

"Please handle this unit with care when taking it out of the box. The sub-woofer in particular, which has the speaker cone located on the bottom of the sub-woofer. If you grab it from the bottom, you could damage it very easily. When set up properly, I found this Sound Bar to have very good sound. However it did take me awhile to reach this state. Because like most men, I know everything, I skipped through the instructions, plugged in the sound bar and was extremely disappointed in the quality of the sound. Here are a few tips to make things easier. If you're doing a horizontal installation in front of the TV at ear level, the sound button the the bar should be located on top, and the small lights that show volume level, etc., should be located on the left when facing your TV. That way the speakers are facing you. Also, I had a difficult time finding the audio settings on my TV to turn off the internal speakers and use the external speakers. Naturally I thought, heck just turn down the volume on the TV speakers to zero and it should be the same thing. Wrong !! You have to find and turn on the external speakers, and turn off the internal speakers for this sound bar to work properly. The sound bar does come with a remote, which is an absolute necessity no matter which sound bar you order. Read the instruction manual carefully, as you have to use the 'previous" and "next" buttons to adjust the Sub-woofer, Bass and Treble settings. Since I know everything, I naturally assumed the volume up and down buttons would adjust these settings. Wrong !! Also, there are buttons to enable TruVolume, and TruSurround HD, but the manual doesn't clarify exactly when to use these settings or what they actually do. I suggest trying both settings and see if you notice any difference in sound quality. I've read a few complaints about the bass not being that strong, but I found it to be excellent. I wonder if these users had the sub-woofer in the correct location, and if they figured out how to raise the sub-woofer level using the remote, and if the sub-woofer stopped working and needed to be "re-linked". I had to re-link mine, and although the instructions could be better, got the sub-woofer working properly in a few minutes. With the sub-woofer is turned on, located in the right area, and adjusted with the remote, you should be very happy with the results. Why only 4 stars for this product? First, the instruction manual could have been more informative about the settings on the remote, and second the ergonomics of the remote are in my opinion very bad. The volume adjustment in particular is usually an up and down toggle on every remote I ever used, but not on this one. The technical designer genius of this remote decided to put a big square "enter/play/pause button between the up and down volume adjustment buttons. Hence adjusting the volume by feel is the worst of any remote I've ever had. That being said, once set up properly, you should be extremely happy with the sound quality of this sound bar."
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO Sound Bar for TV, 28” 2.1 Surround Sound System for TV with Wireless Subwoofer and Bluetooth, Channel Home Theater Sound Bar – Remote SB2821-D6

I find it difficult to type accurately using this keyboard. The keys are higher than those on other keyboards used around here. For example, the keys on the Mac and Acer keyboards are only about 1/8 inch above the underlying keyboard surface. The keys on the Perrix are at least 1/4 inch or more higher than the underlying keyboard surface. This is likely the reason for the difficulty. My hands and fingers are just average size so the logical conclusion is that the height of the keys is the root of the problem.

Other than this one issue, the keyboard is well made, there weren't any dead keys on the unit and the cable is sufficiently long to reach the computer without moving components around.

Should you buy this keyboard? No, if you've got large hands of thick, short fingers. Yes, if you're looking for a cost-effective backup keyboard and can adjust to the higher keys.

Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black) There’s some good points to this bag, but there are also a number of limitations that keep it at a three star rating.

On the plus side, the build quality is, in usual Case Logic fashion, well done. Strong, even stitching throughout; nice straps and buckles; good quality zippers with easy to find pull tabs. It feels and looks quite nice.

Unfortunately, the overall design does not meet as high of a standard. The padding is thin throughout. While I know this is for lighter, smaller DSLRs, I did not feel it provided much security for my Canon Rebel XT with just a couple of lens (50mm and 85mm). It’s not a size issue – just to see if I could, I was able to fit in my Canon 5D Mark II with the Canon 70-200L zoom plus the hood. It’s not a size issue, but rather a padding issue. The foam is thin and is not nearly as dense and bump absorbing as packs from Tenba, Lowepro or Crumpler. Granted, this is addressing a lower price point, but it’s not that low. Other lower-end bags I’ve tried have far more robust padding.

The slot for the tablet is another issue. Great idea; poor execution. There is very little padding for the tablet – forget about putting in a tablet unless it has a hard case, since this backpack won’t offer much protection. Same for the side pockets which have no padding.

This is a good choice if you’re looking to tote very little gear and are willing to bring along the cases for the camera and lenses to aid in keeping them protected. This is not a good choice if you’re looking for a “grab and go” type of backpack. Nice looking, but poor protection.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Pentax K100D Super 6.1MP Digital SLR Camera Shake Reduction and 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Lens First of all, I would like to start with highly recommending this camera to ANYONE who wants premium image quality with expandability, power and flexibility.

Pentax is one of the only companies out there that is driven entirely by photography and NOT by a marketing department that makes outrageous claims. To this end, even this, their lowest-end camera, is PACKED with premium features. Let's take a look at them:

1. Dust Reduction: Dust WILL get into your camera! This keeps it off of the sensor and increases the time inbetween cleanings.

2. Shake Reduction: It's good for a couple of stops of shooting leeway and you get it with every lens you use. Other companies build their systems into the lenses, meaning ONE lens can cost as much or more than the camera, itself! Lens-based anti-shake systems are more effective at long zoom than body-based systems, but unless you're rich, you won't be able to afford a suite of good lenses! With this camera, you can use ANY Pentax lens and get anti-shake.

3. AA batteries: Proprietary battery packs are NO GOOD. Hmmm, if you're on a shoot and your pack dies, you're not taking ANY photos unless you get a spare, right? With this camera, pick up some 2500mAh Ni-MH AA's and you can afford to get three sets. However, the power drain is so small, you might not need more than one set.

4. 6 MP sensor: Don't EVER get trapped in the megapixel hype. Megapixels mean nothing in the DSLR game, except for noise issues. Let me explain. The sensor sizes on almost all DSLRs (except for $5000 full-frame pro cameras) are APS-sized, meaning the sensor size on this camera and the Nikon D300 are very nearly the same dimensions. This means that photosensors on the chip have to be made smaller to get more pixels...meaning that the closer together/smaller sites are LESS light sensitive and they will also interfere with each other. 6 MP is a perfect sweet spot for noise and image sharpness. You get a base ISO of 200, meaning your camera is TWICE as sensitive to light as one with a base ISO of 100! This camera records color accurately and makes prints up to 8.5"x11" with no problem.

This camera has huge features and, even with the release of the K20D and K200D cameras, still maintains a good feature/image quality set with a proven CCD sensor and a suite of easy-to-learn features and settings. I LOVE this camera and even though I have a K200D for the weather sealing and larger burst capacity, the K100D super is the camera I ALWAYS take with me in trips. You're better off getting this camera plus a really nice lens and a 360FZ flash than a more expensive camera with a base kit lens and no external flash.

Believe me, this camera's quality will not fail to impress you and it will grow with you. It can use ANY lens its bigger brothers can and it uses them effortlessly.

A superb camera and one for the record books!
text_fidelity_b: Pentax K100D Super 6.1MP Digital SLR Camera Shake Reduction and 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Lens

text_fidelity_a: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone - Matte Black (Old Model) These headphones do have a more balanced sound than the horrible original Beats that were just too bass heavy. The Bluetooth pairing was quick and easy and battery life is decent. The case and accessories seem to be good quality. In all honesty though for the sound quality I'd never pay the retail asking price for these or recommend them to anyone. I got a used pair (yes they are real Beats) for half the price of new and at this price point I feel it's worth it. The noise canceling isn't anything to write home about and if it's a big reason why you're considering these I'd look to Bose or elsewhere where it's done much better. Another point with these is comfort. They're ok for an hour or so, but I'd not want these on pushing two or more. They tend to pinch at the ear cup level and you can see in various pics how the cups nearly touch when not on the head. So the farther you are pushing those cups out the more they are fighting to close so to speak. I don't have a large head, I don't expand the headband at all when wearing, and they get a little clampy after a bit. Another comfort issue is the interior depth of the ear cups. I don't have big ear or ones that stick out and I still feel my ears slightly pushing against the speaker. I couldn't imagine anyone with large ears being happy with these at all and if you fall into that category I'd definitely try on a pair in a store before buying. The cup pads are nice and it's too bad they didn't make them just a tad deeper.  So in summary these are good headphones if not great ones, but honestly not worth retail. The Bluetooth is nice, but you're obviously paying for image here.
text_fidelity_b: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone - Matte Black (Old Model)

One For All Streamer Remote – Universal Remote Control for up to 3 Devices Infrared Controlled Streamer Boxes TVs and Sound bar – Learning Feature - Backlit Keys - Black – URC7935 I have an LG TV and an ancient Roku 3 purchased in 2015. I’m sick of needed multiple remotes to adjust volume and play media. I also don’t like trying to play guess the button with the Roku remote in the dark.

I ordered this up and got a brief scare when I opened it when it said not for Roku sticks. Only for Roku TVs. What??? Got back on Amazon and looked up compatibility and Roku 3’s are definitely listed as compatible. Is it considered a stick?? Not sure but it’s definitely not a Roku TV.

Anyhow. Setup was pretty easy. It actually came pre programmed to work with my Roku. That took a second to figure out. Programming for the TV only took a few minutes to follow pretty straight forward instructions.

Backlit keys are really nice. I would have put up with the standard mushy silicone keys with the weird over bright green (or blue or red) led shining around the edges.

Instead this had a nice, very subtle light that illuminates the symbol in the middle of the key.

Only con: backlight doesn’t turn on until you actually press a key. It would be more helpful if there was a “turn on the backlight” key that was somehow very distinct feeling. Then once the buttons were lit, I could select the right one.

Hopefully they will do this in their next iteration of this remote. It’s near perfect otherwise.

Edited to add:

After a few days its streamer box functions all stopped working. Tried all the different ways to program it. No dice. Checked if my original Roku remote still worked? It did. New remote still works on TV, just not on Roku. Total bummer. 🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬

text_fidelity_a:
OCTA Spider Monkey - Secure Height Adjustable Stand for iPad, Galaxy, Surface and All Tablets for Desk, Bed, Car, Couch Do I like the Spider Monkey? Yes... with reservations. First let me cover why I like it. I read in bed, and I spend a lot of time switching hands, trying to find ways to prop my book or tablet up, shaking feeling back into my fingers. And then, when I fall asleep, which I always do, the tablet might end up under me or might end up on the floor, and neither is good. The Spider Monkey gives me a way to prop up my tablet without holding it, and to keep it out of my way when I fall asleep.

The downside? How it works depends very much on what you attach it to. I have a headboard that allows me to twist and anchor the tail in a lot of ways, but it doesn't always hold the tablet in position. It can swing around, and be difficult to angle for good reading. Also? It's not all that easy to put together. Once you do, it'll hold, but until then you may find yourself screaming in frustration.

In spite of the drawbacks, though, the Spider Monkey has been a real boon to my reading. If I work with it a bit, it'll even hold my kindle in its cover. I'm not sure I think it's worth $80, to be honest. Half that seems fair to me.

Disclaimer: I received this product in exchange for an honest review.

UPDATE: This morning I got a call from Anthony, from Amazon customer service. First, I was blown away that they would call me to address my issues with Echo Plus. Second, he was knowledgeable, and in no hurry. While it remains to be seen whether every issue with EP is fixed, the problem with Groups was.

It turns out that Alexa didn't like the name I gave my group, it was that simple. My original Echo is black, my EP is white, so I called the group "Black And White". Suggestion: When setting up your groups, go with one of the suggested generic names--bedroom, living room, etc. Echo calls them "Common Names". I called mine "Backyard", even though my backyard isn't involved.

Regarding Alexa often not understanding me on the EP, Anthony suggested that I try switching from British english to American english. I'm going to try that, although I have used British english on my original Echo with no issues.

So, I've upgraded my review to 4 stars, and when and if all issues are resolved I'll be coming back to make it 5. Amazon support definitely gets 5 stars. Even though my first call was a disaster, the way they followed up was remarkable, and that's the important thing. Seriously impressed. Thank you, Anthony!

Epson Home Cinema 5050UB 4K PRO-UHD 3-Chip Projector with HDR,White The 5050ube is an excellent upgrade on the Epson 5040 projector. It provides a significant upgrade on the pseudo-4k projector with an impressive 2600 lumens making it one of the brightest projectors out there easily surpassing the 1500 lumens you would get with the entry level Sony true 4K projector. One of the big upgrades is the move to 18Gbps bandwidth giving you the ability to do 4K at 60Hz. Note that you do need to have a wired connection to get the full 18Gbps -- you only get 12 if you do the wireless option that the 5050ube offers over the regular 5050ub. Even with the reduced bandwidth that you get with the wireless setup, it is a great convenience to have the ability to stream from sources without having to run a wire from the source to the actual projector.

Another great aspect of the 5050 is the motorized lens which is a feature that other more expensive true-4k projectors do not offer. Of course with Epson you do get exceptional HDR quality as well as amazing black.

This is an impressive pseudo-4K projector that provides features that are not even found in some entry level true 4K projectors. If you are not absolutely dying to get true 4k, then this should be one of the projectors you should consider.

text_fidelity_a:
Razer Deathadder Infrared Gaming Mouse Okay, so Razer has a reputation for making products that are of low quality or break prematurely. There may be some truth to that. The "back" button double and triple clicks. I am going to replace the switch.

There is an LED lighted scroll wheel which feels of quality. The sides are a hard smooth plastic. The rest the body is coated with a rubber-like material. There is a lighted Razer logo and I turned off all the LED's.

Even though there is a problem with my mouse I decided to keep it and fix the problem. I have to say that this is probably the most ergonomic, comfortable mouse I have ever used. It has a very high arch and is shaped for a palm grip. I personally don't know if it would be a good gaming mouse ever. The sides are VERY slippery and if you needed a lot of control I don't know if you would have it. Especially if you had to lift off the mouse to readjust, it may slip. In my opinion the Roccat XTD Kone is the best mouse I have ever used. It is very big and heavy and there are grooves for your thumb and outer fingers. It feels more sturdy.

The reason I gave it 3 stars instead of 4, the mouse is always a little warm to the touch and it seems to absorb heat from your hand and get hotter. The Roccat mouse is made from similar materials and always feels cool. I have heard that there are parts of the circuitry that generate more heat than normal. So in summary, I like it for general use. If I was gaming or doing something that requires precision such as graphic design I would use the Roccat Kone XTD.

Edit: follow up- I have owned this mouse now for 3 weeks and I have it next to the Roccat mouse. I should share that I have used the Razer almost exclusively and switched to the Roccat only when I needed to use forward and back buttons (they are hard to reach on Razer). I think the Razer is more comfortable to rest your hand on for long periods at a time. However, it just seems that I have better control of the right click, left click, and forward-back buttons. The DA causes your hand to form an arch, while your hand is more flat with the Roccat. I wonder if your index finger is in a stronger postion with the Roccat; it feels so.
text_fidelity_b: Razer Deathadder Infrared Gaming Mouse

text_fidelity_a:
iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey This is advertised as a 'sleeve for a 13" laptop' which is such an understatement. Not only will this hold a laptop up to 14 inches, it also has compartments for a cell phone, an IPad or other tablet device (my Kindle fits in there quite nicely) and all the necessary chargers and earphones, making this a one stop transportation and storage device for all personal electronics. There is even a bit of room left over to tuck a newspaper, or a file or two. And, unlike most sleeves, this has handles and an optional shoulder strap.

The compartments are zippered so things should not spill out too easily (although I would open the compartment holding the chargers cautiously). It is a nice, neutral grey color that should not make anyone feel self conscious about carrying it and seems to be reasonably durable. The various compartments seem to be adequately padded against the normal traumas (I don't think I would count on it to protect my computer if it were dropped).

There are a few issues though. First since it is not a typical sleeve it probably would not easily fit into a backpack. Second, fully loaded with a computer, phone, tablet and chargers it will be heavy enough that handling this plus a backpack or briefcase during a commute could be awkward. Third, having everything in one spot could be convenient for travelers except dragging everything out to go through TSA and then repacking it would be time consuming.

Overall this is a great product.

text_fidelity_a:
Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black Like everyone in California, we've been having a lot of power outages and spotty power, and through that, I've been really made aware how important it is to have steady, continuous power to my devices and not be affected by brownouts or power surges. I also really appreciate that when the power goes out suddenly, I have enough time to save my work, print a document, or do any last critical wrap up before things go dark. This battery backup has been great!

If you have used battery backup in the past you generally know what to expect, you plug it into the wall, plug in your devices, and when the power goes out you have a little bit of time, depending on which devices are sapping power from it and how much juice they take, to finish up what you are doing and shut down properly.

What is interesting to me about this one is that it has something that automatically powers down accessory devices like your monitor or scanner when the master device is off. So I have the one plug for the master device, which is my computer, and one plug that is on battery backup that will power down and accessory device like my monitor when my computer is not on, and three plugs that will power down accessory devices and not have them on battery backup, good for things like my scanner. While I haven't hooked up a power reader to determine exactly my savings, I do know for sure that some of these accessory devices are indeed using power when they are not being used, so I really appreciate the thoughtfulness of this.

There are also some regular plugs, some of which are battery backup and some not. This is perfect because there are ample plugs for everything and I can really set things up just the way I need so that my printer is not drawing battery power during a power outage unless I actually want it to.

It's working as expected and seems to be designed with care. I definitely recommend this.
text_fidelity_b: Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black

This isn’t really a problem per se, but it is quite finicky and it the only part of the operation my wife had to assist with. I included two pics with this review that I took while in the process of getting it and components situated. The stand easily fits my vintage Sansui 661 receiver on the middle shelf and Audio Technica LP120 turntable on the top. I hope both this review and photos showing it with the perspective of having components on it help.

Edit: So, yea, I did dock a star due to the feet issue. As I noted they are finicky, but can quickly get frustrating. While I had to move the stand around getting my stereo stuff sorted the small discs constantly came off and you just really can’t put them back in solo. They will and did put small indentations on my floor with the discs off. My solution was to pick up a 4 pack of 1” sliders from WM that are plastic on the bottom with an adhesive disc on the top. I then stuck the small metal discs from the stand on the slider. Once my wife helped me place the discs back on the legs it could then slide pretty freely and they stayed on. It’s a shame they didn’t include a normal leg along with the pins. I still like the stand quite a bit, but I’d warn people with mobility issues against this one even as nice as it is.

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I am a big fan of my kindles. I have the kindle keyboard ereaders 1st and 3rd gen , the 2nd gen Fire 8.9" and last year I bought the 6" Fire. I would not have bought this one except that my 6" Fire has gotten glitchy. I have not had problems with any of my kindles before so I chalked it up to just a bad egg.
I was thinking of replacing it when I found this great deal on the lastest 7" Fire. $100 for a tablet is such a deal. $50 is AMAZING!!
There isn't a huge difference other than this one is a little bigger. It was easy to import everything from my old tablet to my new one. My books, photos, songs, even my book marks from Silk. The set up took minutes.
The home page is different, it looks like the ones on iphones with all the apps on the home page. You can group them into smaller collections, you can also upload your own photo to be the wallpaper. I like this better than the carousel. You can also group your books into collections. There is a button so that you can move between applications without them closing out. It will show all the last places you went so you can pick up where you were and just switch screens. This is my favorite new feature, even more than the change with the home screen.
I'm not super fond of Silk but it is less annoying since they did an upgrade.
I have only had one problem: when I was first setting it up, the screen kept freezing. I rebooted it and I haven't had an issue since.
This is just as fast as my 6" tablet. Battery usage seems the same as well. According to the specs this should be a little slower than the 6" with less battery time but I have not noticed a difference. The plastic back feels only a little less durable than my other kindles but I'm not concerned. I feel like I have gotten quite a deal.
The camera isn't really improved since there isn't a flash and the sound quality is the same as well. Movies look great. I'm really happy that I can add a memory card. Movies, music, and audio books use a lot of memory but now I'll have more memory than I need.
You are getting so much for your money. I've never used other brand tablets, I'm not an Apple user. They may or may not be better but are their prices worth it?
I love Prime access for music and videos and that they can be downloaded.
I'm very happy with my new tablet!

text_fidelity_a:
AUDIANO 8K HDMI 2.1 Cable, 48 Gbps Ultra High Speed 3D Nylon Braided Cord, Supports 8K 60Hz 4K 120Hz 144Hz, eARC Dolby Vision HDR 10, HDCP 2.2 2.3, Compatible with Roku/PS4/PS5/Blu-ray(10ft/3M) I'm aware of the benefits of a 2.1 cable. I bought 2 sets to prepare for my incoming PS5 which also has HDMI 2.1. I did not see any benefits like high speed switching, extra colors etc it did pass the standard Audio, HDR etc. The cable itself is built well, solid and the connection feels premium.

Than, I noticed the bottle neck, my home theater receiver, which I bought randomly in 2019 before HDMI 2.1 was out lacked it to complete the link to TV. I bought a new HDTV in 2020 that has HDMI 2.1 connection. Since I had everything in the receiver, and out to TV. The receiver could not pass the 2.1 or some 2.0 bonuses. As soon as I connected my PS4 PRO directly to the tv, the colors were made available. Even my PS4 PRO system menu stated that I could get higher res, colors and hertz (60 options variable) and showed them listed with HDR and without. TP-LINK TL-PA511 KIT AV500 Powerline Gigabit Adapter Starter Kit, up to 500Mbps The TP-Link Powerline Adapter is a great kit for spanning distances or to help boost the signal of a router in the home. What this does is take the signal from your modem or router and transmits it over your power lines, and this allows you to have signal where you might otherwise have environmental issues blocking a wireless signal such as concrete, steel beams or just distance. One of the major drawbacks to this product is that the plugs you are using must be on the same circuit, though most people shouldn't run into this issue.

One of the biggest issues I have with this product is the fact that it isn't plug and play, not by the true definition. You HAVE to run the software to get your computer to recognize the plugs. I attempted to use them without running the software first and my computer couldn't connect to my home network. After running the software, it connected no problem. So Please take note: THIS IS NOT TRUE PLUG AND PLAY.

These are Gigabit (please note "Gigabit" is not the same as "Gigabyte") adapters and work very well. I was able to watch Youtube.com and Hulu without any issues. The web pages loaded as quickly as if I were directly connected to my router or on my wifi network.

Pros:

-Great for Larger houses to get a better signal for the home network.
-Good for streaming and downloads.
-Creates a good enough connection to act as if you are directly connected to the modem/router.

Cons:

-MUST be on the same circuit!
-Can't use a surge strip or UPS(uninterruptable power source) with these adapters so there is a risk of electrical shock to your computer during a storm.
-NOT TRUE Plug and Play. YOU MUST RUN THE SOFTWARE FIRST.

3.5 stars
text_fidelity_b: TP-LINK TL-PA511 KIT AV500 Powerline Gigabit Adapter Starter Kit, up to 500Mbps

Kensington Orbit® Fusion™ Wireless Trackball (K72363WW), Black I used a Logitech M570, a thumb trackball, for years until I started gaming again and needed a gaming mouse. Now I’m done with gaming for a while and have been searching for a trackball to reduce strain.

The Kensington Orbit Fusion Wireless Trackball is the first Kensington trackball I’ve tried.

I hate the scroll ring. I think this is either a feature you love or hate, and well, I just don’t like it. Using the scroll ring is uncomfortable for me; I keep going back to my laptop trackpad instead of using it. It’s too easy to move the trackball while using the scroll ring, and I couldn’t decide which finger was most comfortable for using it. I spent a lot of time fiddling with the scrolling speed in the KensingtonWorks program, but content doesn’t move smoothly on my screen -- it jumps.

The mouse is too big for my hand. I usually wear a size small in women’s winter and nitrile gloves, to give an idea of the size. My fingers have to stretch too much to reach the left and right click buttons at the same time. My hand rises off the mouse when I use the scroll ring.

I know some of this is muscle memory, but my wrist and hand actually hurt after using the trackball for more than a few minutes.

I do like that KensingtonWorks can be used on Windows or Mac. I’ve tried a lot of high end gaming mice that I can’t always customize on my Mac. KensingtonWorks lets you modify the pointer, scroll ring, and customize the buttons. You can also back up your settings to Google Drive or Microsoft OneDrive, and set options for specific programs. Kensington also included a USB-A to USB-C adapter.

The USB ports are dated and are not worth it unless you want to charge small devices and only one, maybe two at a time.
This "Surge Protector" has an FCC emblem imprinted on the back, which may be illegal, not sure, but does not actually have the required holographic sticker to prove that it's safe or certified. I'm not sure it's either one.
"If" I were to use this, I would only use this for low wattage electric items that are inexpensive to replace and would not consider it a "Surge Protector" at all. I would also always unplug it when I was finished using it and not leave it plugged in.
All of my surge protectors have the FCC stickers and most also have information on the cord itself. This one has all the specs you see in the listing and says it's a surge protector on the back.
This would be a great deal if it had certification and came with a good warranty, but it doesn't. If you're a gambler and like to take chances, buy it. If not, look for a real surge protector that has protection to back it, and your devices if it fails. Not to mention, this thing might burn your house down one day. I don't think I will be using it for much, if at all, and I would not recommend It, as it is just too risky. 3 stars ✨

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500) Compared to the Crucial 1TB M2 NVME I reviewed earlier, this Sabrent 512GB model benchmarks a little faster. And it works just fine on a PCI M2 adapter card, which are only a few bucks. (I bought the cheapest one available and it works.)

The NVME still offers much faster R/W speeds than other drives even when used with SATA 1 (as on my workstation). For example, the SSD I was using as my hard disk benchmarks at about 220MB/second. The Sabrent NVME on a PCI card benchmarks at about 1.5GB/second.

This time I experimented to see if I could get Debian Linux distro running on the NVME on my older workstation.

It took a few tries. Getting the OS to boot directly from the NVME was a no-go. Since the NVME is mounted on an adapter card, I had hoped it would trick the system into thinking it was just an ordinary SATA drive and boot from it. But that didn't happen.

So what I did was installed all the Linux OS EXCEPT for the boot folder on the NVME, and put the boot folder on the SSD HDD. So it boots from the SSD but the entire OS is on the NVME and runs from it.

Step one:

The partition manager in the Debian installer didn't want to partition the NVME at first.

So I bailed out of it and used GParted (Gnome disks utility couldn't do this) to "create partition table" and selected msdos as type. That wiped everything and turned the whole drive into unallocated space. From that point the partition manager worked.

Step two:

From the linux bootable USB installer I partitioned the SSD (not the NVME) with a primary partition labeled (to be mounted) as /boot. (You can make this partition most any size from a few GB on up---the boot files don't require a lot of space.) The remaining space I manually labeled as /msc.

I partitioned the NVME so the installer would put everything else on it, starting with / (root). You can simply make the whole NVME / root and the installer will take care of putting everything else on that drive, or you can do what I did and set up size-defined partitions for /home, /usr, and so on.

After installing the system, the installer asks where you want the bootloader GRUB installed. I selected the SSD.

It worked. The SSD does the booting to the NVME, which then runs the OS. And it did improve speed.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500)
